definition: Assenting e: the thought episode e takes its content to be so (an assent or judgment), as opposed to merely entertaining, doubting, willing or imagining it. Example: judging that the stove is hot. Non-examples: wishing it were warmer; doubting whether the stove is hot. In Lean a parameter Episode -> Prop, constrained only by STMT-COGITO-OCCURRING-THOUGHT-IS-ASSENTING and STMT-ASSENTING-BEARER-OPINES-CONTENT.
note: Stipulative analyst notion, attribution deferred. The claim that every occurring thought is assenting is false on Descartes's broad cogitatio (willing, doubting) and is carried as the open premise STMT-COGITO-OCCURRING-THOUGHT-IS-ASSENTING; its omission model is a borne willing (NonAssentingThought).
